questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It protects your whole face.
It does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not your entire face. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: On short trips.
On long trips.
After at least one hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles. These crashes occur just a few minutes after the rider starts out.

questions.question: If you carry a load in a sidecar, what happens to the motorcycle's stopping distance?

options.text: It may increase.
It may decrease.
It is not a concern.
It stays the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Adding a load to a motorcycle increases its weight. This extra weight makes the motorcycle harder to stop, so stopping distance may increase. Start slowing down earlier when riding with a load or passenger in a sidecar.

questions.question: What should you NOT do to stay safe when riding at night?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Reduce your speed.
Use your high beam headlight when possible.
Increase your following distance.

questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, use your high beam headlight when no other vehicles are near, and increase your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead of you—their headlights help light the road, and their taillights show if there are bumps ahead.

questions.question: When should you use a larger cushion of space between you and other vehicles?

options.text: When roads are slippery.
When it is sunny.
When it is cold.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.explanation: A two-second following distance is normally adequate. Use a larger cushion of space when conditions increase your stopping distance, such as wet or icy roads.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain.
Take artificial stimulants.
Limit how far you ride in one day.
Take frequent breaks.

questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks to rest and do not ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain, as these make you tire quickly. Do not use artificial stimulants—when they wear off, it can be very dangerous.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: Far from home.
On short trips.
On long rides.
Several hours into the ride.

questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles. These happen just a few minutes after the rider starts out.

questions.question: Which provides the best face protection?

options.text: Sunglasses
Windshield
Goggles
Face shield

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes, not your whole face. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent

questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when being passed?

options.text: In the center portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
Weave between all three portions of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases your crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to merge back too early.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. They tell you the rules of the road. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When riding in a group while passing another vehicle, it is best to:

options.text: Allow one rider to fully pass the other vehicle before another rider begins to pass.
Allow several members of the group to pass the other vehicle at once.
Have the last rider in the group wave to the driver being passed to signal that no other motorcycles are approaching.
Pass in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow one rider to fully pass the other vehicle before another rider begins to pass.
questions.explanation: In a group, one rider should pass at a time. Each rider must finish passing and get back into formation before the next rider begins to pass.

questions.question: A shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Can protect a rider's face in a crash.
Is only useful in protecting riders from dirt.
Does not offer as much protection as goggles.
Should not be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect a rider's face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and rocks.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Protect your lane from other drivers.
Allow you a nice view of scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your intentions from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your lane from other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position keeps you out of blind spots, helps other drivers see you, helps you avoid hazards, protects you from wind blasts, and gives you an escape route. Your position should discourage other drivers from entering your lane.

questions.question: If using a sidecar to transport a load, you should:

options.text: Allow the load to move freely.
Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
Place the load unsecured in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
questions.explanation: Loads in a sidecar must be secured so they do not move and affect how the motorcycle handles. Place the load toward the back of the sidecar to prevent the sidecar nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: A helmet will not provide the best possible protection:

options.text: If it is certified by the DOT.
If it fits snugly.
If it is free of defects.
If it has cracks.

questions.explanation: A helmet must have a DOT certification and fit snugly to protect you well. It should have no damage like cracks, loose padding, or broken straps.

questions.question: Riding directly alongside another vehicle:

options.text: Can place you in the driver's blind spot.
Is better than riding behind the other vehicle.
Is safe because it limits your escape routes.
Should only be done during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can place you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride directly beside another vehicle. The driver may not see you and could move into your lane without warning. Riding beside a vehicle also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: The pass may be completed in a no passing zone.
The rider may travel up to 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
The pass must be started and completed within a passing zone.
The pass must be completed on the shoulder, if one is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pass must be started and completed within a passing zone.
questions.explanation: You must start and finish passing only in areas marked for passing. Always stay at or below the speed limit while passing.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the front brake first.
Throttle down and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Plans to turn left.
Is about to stop.
Plans to turn right.
Is about to slow down.

questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals instead of turn signals. When a rider's left arm is straight out, it means they plan to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Only a front brake.
Only a rear brake.
Brakes on both the front and rear.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes on both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have two brakes. One controls the front wheel and one controls the rear wheel.

questions.question: Braking while turning is:

options.text: Easier than braking on a straight road.
Harder than braking on a straight road.
Safe if you use only the front brake.
Safe if you use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking while turning is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must know the correct technique and be very careful.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Use only one brake in non-emergency situations.
Use both brakes only when riding on wet roads.
Use both brakes every time, no matter what.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes every time, no matter what.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.explanation: The rear brake pedal is located near the right footrest.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve:

options.text: Riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
Faulty ignition systems.
Distractions caused by passengers.
Riding at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a motorcycle you are new to. Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders who have had their bike for less than six months.
